questions.q: When a glass rod is rubbed with silk, the rod becomes positively charged because
options: electrons move from the silk to the glass
electrons move from the glass to the silk
protons move from the glass to the silk
protons move from the silk to the glass
questions.explanation: Glass loses electrons to silk, leaving it with a net positive charge; protons do not move in rubbing.

questions.q: The electrostatic force between two point charges placed in a medium of dielectric constant K, compared with that in vacuum at the same separation, is
questions.explanation: F_medium = F_vacuum/K.

questions.q: An electron is placed in a uniform electric field of 2 × 10^4 N/C. The magnitude of the force on it is (e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C)
A closed surface encloses a charge of 17.7 nC. The net electric flux through it is (ε0 = 8.85 × 10^-12 C²/N m²)
A total charge Q is divided into two parts q and (Q - q) which are then separated by a fixed distance. The force between them is greatest when q equals
questions.explanation: F is proportional to q(Q - q), which has its maximum at q = Q/2.

questions.q: The electric field inside the cavity of a charged hollow conducting sphere (with no charge in the cavity) is zero because
options: a Gaussian surface in the cavity encloses no charge and all the charge lies on the outer surface
the charges cancel pairwise at every point inside
field lines are bent around the cavity
questions.explanation: In equilibrium the charge sits on the outer surface, so by Gauss's law the enclosed charge for any surface in the cavity is zero.

questions.q: Find the force between charges +4 μC and -5 μC placed 0.3 m apart in air (k = 9 × 10^9 N m²/C²). State whether it is attractive or repulsive.
questions.explanation: Opposite signs mean the force is attractive.

questions.q: Charges +2 μC and -2 μC are 20 cm apart in air. Find the electric field at the midpoint of the line joining them (k = 9 × 10^9 N m²/C²).
questions.answer: 3.6 × 10^6 N/C, directed from the positive towards the negative charge.
keyPoints: Each charge is 0.1 m away and gives kq/r² = 1.8 × 10^6 N/C
Both fields point the same way (towards the negative charge)
questions.explanation: At the midpoint the two contributions add.

questions.q: The energy stored per unit volume in an electric field E in vacuum is
questions.explanation: The electric energy density is u = ½ε0E².

questions.q: The electric field is directed
questions.explanation: E = -dV/dr, so the field points in the direction of decreasing potential.

questions.q: A 5 μF capacitor holds a charge of 2.5 × 10^-4 C. The potential difference across it is
The electric potential at 0.3 m from a point charge of -6 μC is (k = 9 × 10^9 N m²/C²)
A parallel plate capacitor is charged and disconnected from the battery. The plates are then pulled apart to double their separation. The stored energy
questions.explanation: Q is fixed and C halves, so U = Q²/2C doubles (the extra energy comes from the work done pulling the plates).

questions.q: Two identical capacitors of capacitance C are joined in parallel, and this pair is joined in series with a third identical capacitor. The equivalent capacitance is
questions.explanation: Parallel pair = 2C; in series with C gives (2C × C)/(3C) = 2C/3.

questions.q: Find the energy stored in a 2 μF capacitor charged to 200 V.
questions.explanation: Substitute C and V in ½CV².

questions.q: Point A is at a potential of +30 V and point B at -20 V. How much work does the electric field do in moving a charge of +5 μC from A to B?
questions.answer: 2.5 × 10^-4 J, positive work done by the field.
questions.explanation: A positive charge moves naturally from high to low potential, so the field does positive work.

questions.q: Electric current is the rate of flow of
questions.explanation: I = dq/dt.

questions.q: Which of the following does not obey Ohm's law?
options: A copper wire at constant temperature
A nichrome wire at constant temperature
A silver wire at constant temperature
questions.explanation: The current through a diode is not proportional to the voltage, so it is a non-ohmic device.

questions.q: Three identical 6 Ω resistors can be combined to give a total of 9 Ω by connecting
options: two in series and this pair in parallel with the third
two in parallel and this pair in series with the third
questions.explanation: Two in parallel give 3 Ω, and 3 + 6 = 9 Ω in series with the third.

questions.q: A current of 0.5 A flows for 10 minutes. The charge that passes is
A battery of emf 6 V and internal resistance 1 Ω is connected to a variable load. The maximum power that can be delivered to the load is
questions.explanation: Maximum power occurs when R = r: P = E²/4r = 36/4 = 9 W.

questions.q: Two wires of the same material have lengths in the ratio 1 : 2 and radii in the ratio 1 : 2. The ratio of their resistances R1 : R2 is
questions.explanation: R is proportional to l/r²: (1/1²)/(2/2²) = 1/(1/2) = 2, so R1 : R2 = 2 : 1.

questions.q: Distinguish between the emf of a cell and its terminal voltage.
questions.answer: The emf is the potential difference between the terminals when no current is drawn (open circuit). The terminal voltage is the potential difference when current I flows, and equals ε - Ir, so it is less than the emf while the cell is delivering current.
keyPoints: emf is the open-circuit potential difference
Terminal voltage V = ε - Ir during discharge
V equals ε only when I = 0
questions.explanation: The drop across the internal resistance accounts for the difference.

questions.q: Four identical cells, each of emf 1.5 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω, supply a 4 Ω resistor. Find the current when the cells are connected (a) in series and (b) in parallel.
keyPoints: Series: ε = 6 V, r = 2 Ω so I = 6/(4 + 2) = 1 A
questions.explanation: Series grouping is better when the external resistance is larger than the internal resistance.

questions.q: Two long parallel wires carry currents in opposite directions. They
options: exert no force on each other
questions.explanation: Opposite currents repel; parallel currents attract.

questions.q: A device used to accelerate charged particles to high energies using a magnetic field and an alternating electric field is the
questions.explanation: The cyclotron accelerates particles each time they cross the gap between the dees.

questions.q: A circular loop of radius 0.1 m carries a current of 2 A. Its magnetic moment is
The magnetic field at the centre of a semicircular wire of radius R carrying current I is
questions.explanation: A full loop gives μ0I/2R, so a half loop gives half of it, μ0I/4R.

questions.q: A proton and a deuteron (same charge, twice the mass) enter the same uniform magnetic field with the same speed, perpendicular to it. The ratio of the radii of their paths r_p : r_d is
questions.explanation: r = mv/(qB) is proportional to the mass at equal q and v, so the ratio is 1 : 2.

questions.q: A cyclotron with a magnetic field of 1 T and dee radius 0.5 m accelerates protons. The maximum kinetic energy is closest to (e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C, m = 1.67 × 10^-27 kg)
Two long parallel wires 0.2 m apart carry currents of 4 A and 5 A in the same direction. Find the force per unit length between them (μ0/4π = 10^-7 T m/A).
questions.explanation: Substitute the currents and separation.

questions.q: An electron moves at 2 × 10^6 m/s at 60° to a uniform magnetic field of 0.01 T. Find the pitch of its helical path (m = 9.1 × 10^-31 kg, e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C).
keyPoints: Component along B: v∥ = v cos60° = 10^6 m/s
questions.explanation: The pitch is the distance moved along the field in one revolution.

questions.q: The magnetic susceptibility of a diamagnetic substance is
questions.explanation: Diamagnets develop a weak magnetisation opposite to the applied field.

questions.q: A material suitable for making a permanent magnet should have
questions.explanation: It must stay strongly magnetised and resist demagnetisation.

questions.q: A material has H = 1000 A/m and magnetisation M = 3000 A/m. Taking μ0 = 4π × 10^-7 T m/A, the magnetic field B is
If the distance from a short bar magnet along its axis is doubled, the axial magnetic field becomes
questions.explanation: For a short magnet B is proportional to 1/r³, so doubling r gives 1/8.

questions.q: A compass needle that can rotate freely only in a horizontal plane is placed at a magnetic pole of the Earth. It
options: can rest in any direction because the horizontal field is zero
questions.explanation: At the pole the dip is 90° and the horizontal component is zero, so there is no torque to align the needle.

questions.q: The magnetic susceptibility of a superconductor, which behaves as a perfect diamagnet, is
questions.explanation: It expels the magnetic field completely (Meissner effect), so B = 0 inside and χ = -1.

questions.q: Define magnetic susceptibility and relative permeability and give the relation between them.
questions.answer: Magnetic susceptibility χ is the ratio of the magnetisation to the magnetising field, χ = M/H. Relative permeability μr is the ratio μ/μ0 = B/(μ0H). They are related by μr = 1 + χ.
questions.explanation: Since B = μ0(H + M) = μ0(1 + χ)H.

questions.q: A small bar magnet of moment of inertia 2 × 10^-5 kg m² and magnetic moment 0.5 A m² oscillates in a field of 0.4 T. Find its time period for small oscillations.
questions.explanation: A stronger field or larger moment shortens the period.

questions.q: The emf induced in a rotating coil in a uniform magnetic field is maximum when the plane of the coil is
questions.explanation: The flux is zero but changing most rapidly when the plane is parallel to B.

questions.q: Eddy current losses in a transformer core are reduced by
questions.explanation: Thin insulated laminations break up the paths of the eddy currents.

questions.q: The flux linked with a coil is Φ = (2t² + 3t) Wb, with t in seconds. The induced emf at t = 2 s is
questions.explanation: |ε| = dΦ/dt = 4t + 3 = 11 V at t = 2 s.

questions.q: A long solenoid has 1000 turns, cross-sectional area 2 × 10^-4 m² and length 0.5 m. Its self-inductance is (μ0 = 4π × 10^-7 T m/A)
The energy density of the magnetic field in a region where B = 0.1 T (in air, μ0 = 4π × 10^-7 T m/A) is closest to
A rod 0.5 m long slides at 2 m/s on frictionless rails in a perpendicular field of 0.4 T. The circuit has a total resistance of 0.4 Ω. The external force needed to keep the speed constant is
Distinguish between self-inductance and mutual inductance.
questions.answer: Self-inductance relates the emf induced in a coil to the changing current in that same coil, ε = -L dI/dt. Mutual inductance relates the emf induced in one coil to the changing current in a neighbouring coil, ε2 = -M dI1/dt. Both are measured in henry.
keyPoints: Self: induced in the same coil by its own current change
Mutual: induced in a second coil by the first coil's current change
questions.explanation: They depend on geometry and the medium.

questions.q: An aircraft wing of span 30 m flies horizontally at 250 m/s where the vertical component of the Earth's field is 5 × 10^-5 T. Find the emf induced between the wing tips.
questions.explanation: The wing sweeps through vertical field lines like a moving rod.

questions.q: A transformer works on the principle of
questions.explanation: A changing current in the primary induces an emf in the secondary through their mutual inductance.

questions.q: A step-up transformer has
options: more turns in the secondary than in the primary
fewer turns in the secondary than in the primary
a direct current in the primary
questions.explanation: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np, so a larger Ns raises the voltage.

questions.q: The rms value of mains voltage is 220 V. Its peak value is closest to
The average value of a sinusoidal alternating current over one full cycle is
questions.explanation: The positive and negative half cycles cancel.

questions.q: A 220 V, 50 Hz supply is applied across a resistor of 100 Ω in series with an inductor of (1/π) H. The phase angle between voltage and current is
questions.explanation: X_L = 2π × 50 × (1/π) = 100 Ω, so tanφ = X_L/R = 1 and φ = 45°, with current lagging.

questions.q: A series LCR circuit is driven at a frequency below its resonant frequency. The circuit behaves as
questions.explanation: Below resonance X_C = 1/ωC is larger than X_L = ωL, so the net reactance is capacitive.

questions.q: Define the rms value of an alternating current and state its relation to the peak value for a sinusoidal current.
questions.answer: The rms value of an alternating current is the value of a steady current that produces the same heating effect in a resistor as the alternating current over a cycle. For a sinusoidal current I_rms = I0/√2 ≈ 0.707 I0.
keyPoints: Equal heating effect to a steady direct current
Root mean square of the current over a cycle
questions.explanation: The average of sin² over a cycle is ½, giving the factor 1/√2.

questions.q: A transformer is 90% efficient. Its primary draws 5 A at 220 V and the secondary voltage is 22 V. Find the secondary current.
questions.explanation: Efficiency is the ratio of output power to input power.

questions.q: Electromagnetic waves were first produced and detected in the laboratory by
questions.explanation: Heinrich Hertz generated and detected radio waves in 1887, confirming Maxwell's prediction.

questions.q: Which electromagnetic radiation is used in water purifiers to kill germs?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet radiation damages the DNA of microorganisms.

questions.q: Which of these wavelengths lies in the visible part of the spectrum?
questions.explanation: Visible light spans roughly 400 nm to 700 nm.

questions.q: The speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum is related to the permeability μ0 and permittivity ε0 of free space by
questions.explanation: Maxwell's equations give c = 1/√(μ0ε0).

questions.q: A microwave oven operates at a frequency of 2.45 GHz. The wavelength of the waves in air is closest to (c = 3 × 10^8 m/s)
The photon energy of electromagnetic radiation of wavelength 0.1 nm is (hc = 1240 eV nm)
questions.explanation: E = 1240 eV nm/0.1 nm = 12400 eV = 12.4 keV, in the X-ray region.

questions.q: Why are microwaves used in radar systems?
questions.answer: Microwaves have short wavelengths, so they can be formed into narrow, directional beams by small antennas. They are reflected well by aircraft, ships and rain, and the time taken by the echo gives the distance of the object.
keyPoints: Short wavelength gives narrow, directional beams
Reflected by objects such as aircraft
questions.explanation: These properties let radar locate and track objects.

questions.q: The plates of a parallel plate capacitor have area 0.01 m². The electric field between them is changing at 5 × 10^12 V/(m s). Find the displacement current (ε0 = 8.85 × 10^-12 C²/N m²).
keyPoints: I_d = ε0 dΦ_E/dt = ε0 A dE/dt
questions.explanation: This equals the conduction current charging the capacitor.

questions.q: A real image is one that
options: cannot be obtained on a screen
is formed by diverging rays only
is formed where rays actually meet and can be caught on a screen
questions.explanation: A real image is formed by actual convergence of rays.

questions.q: In the Cartesian sign convention, the focal length of a concave mirror is
questions.explanation: Distances measured against the incident light are negative, and the focus of a concave mirror is in front of it.

questions.q: A ray of light enters glass of refractive index √3 from air at an angle of incidence of 60°. The angle of refraction is
For light going from water (refractive index 4/3) to air, sin of the critical angle is
An object is placed 20 cm in front of a concave lens of focal length 20 cm. The image is
options: 10 cm from the lens on the same side as the object, virtual
10 cm from the lens on the other side, real
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = -1/20 - 1/20 = -1/10, so v = -10 cm, a virtual image on the object's side (m = +0.5).

questions.q: A thin convex lens of focal length f is cut into two halves by a plane containing the principal axis. Each half has a focal length of
questions.explanation: The curvatures are unchanged, so f is the same; only the brightness of the image is reduced.

questions.q: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 40 cm. An object is placed 30 cm in front of it. Find the position and magnification of the image.
questions.answer: The image is 60 cm in front of the mirror, real and inverted, with magnification -2.
questions.explanation: The object lies between F and C, so the image is real, inverted, enlarged and beyond C.

questions.q: The far point of a myopic person is 80 cm. What is the power of the lens needed to see distant objects clearly?
questions.answer: -1.25 D (a concave lens of focal length 80 cm).
keyPoints: The lens must form an image of a distant object at the far point, 80 cm
questions.explanation: A diverging lens brings the image of infinity to the far point.

questions.q: The colours seen in a thin soap film are due to
questions.explanation: Light reflected from the two surfaces of the film interferes.

questions.q: According to the wave theory, the speed of light in a denser medium compared with a rarer medium is
questions.explanation: Huygens' wave construction gives v = c/n, which is smaller for a denser medium.

questions.q: Two waves interfere destructively when their path difference is λ/2. Their phase difference is
questions.explanation: Phase difference = 2π/λ × path difference = π.

questions.q: Two coherent beams, each of intensity I0, meet with a phase difference of 120°. The resultant intensity is
questions.explanation: I = 4I0 cos²(φ/2) = 4I0 cos²60° = I0.

questions.q: In a double slit experiment the fringe width is 0.5 mm. The distance between the 5th bright fringe and the 2nd dark fringe on the same side of the centre is
questions.explanation: The 5th bright is at 5β = 2.5 mm and the 2nd dark at 1.5β = 0.75 mm, so the separation is 1.75 mm.

questions.q: Light reflected from the surface of water of refractive index 4/3 is completely polarised when the angle of incidence is closest to
questions.explanation: tan i_B = 4/3, so i_B ≈ 53°.

questions.q: Why do two independent sodium lamps not produce a sustained interference pattern?
questions.answer: The light from separate atoms is emitted in random, short bursts, so the phase difference between the two lamps changes randomly and rapidly. The sources are therefore not coherent and the fringe pattern keeps shifting and averages out to uniform illumination.
keyPoints: Phase changes randomly about every 10^-10 s
questions.explanation: Sustained interference needs a constant phase difference.

questions.q: Light of wavelength 500 nm falls on a single slit and produces a central maximum 2 cm wide on a screen 2 m away. Find the width of the slit.
questions.explanation: Rearranging the single-slit width formula gives the slit width.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depends on
options: the frequency of the light and the metal used
the area of the emitting surface
questions.explanation: K_max = hf - φ, depending on f and the work function.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: The rest mass of a photon is
questions.explanation: A photon has energy and momentum but zero rest mass.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: Using λ(Å) = 12.27/√V, the de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through 1 V is

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: Sodium has a work function of 2.3 eV. Light of wavelength 400 nm (photon energy 3.1 eV, from hc = 1240 eV nm) falls on it. The maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: A 4 eV photon produces photoelectrons with a stopping potential of 1.5 V on a given metal. For a 6 eV photon on the same metal the stopping potential is
questions.explanation: The work function is 4 - 1.5 = 2.5 eV, so for a 6 eV photon K_max = 3.5 eV and V0 = 3.5 V.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: An electron and a photon both have a wavelength of 1 Å. Which has the greater energy?
questions.explanation: The photon energy is hc/λ ≈ 12.4 keV, whereas the electron's kinetic energy is only about 150 eV.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: State three observations of the photoelectric effect that the wave theory of light cannot explain.
questions.answer: (1) There is a threshold frequency below which no emission occurs, however intense the light. (2) The maximum kinetic energy of the electrons depends on the frequency and not on the intensity. (3) Emission is instantaneous, with no measurable time delay even at low intensity.
questions.explanation: Einstein's photon picture explains all three.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: Using λ(Å) = 12.27/√V, find the de Broglie wavelength of electrons accelerated through 54 V, as in the Davisson-Germer experiment.
questions.explanation: This matched the wavelength deduced from the diffraction peak.

questions.q: The ionisation energy of a hydrogen atom in its ground state is
questions.explanation: It is the energy needed to take the electron from n = 1 to infinity.

questions.q: Which of the radiations from radioactive substances is the most penetrating?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays are uncharged photons and pass through thick material.

questions.q: Uranium-238 (Z = 92) decays to lead-206 (Z = 82) through a series of decays. The numbers of alpha and beta-minus particles emitted are
questions.explanation: ΔA = 32 means 8 alpha particles, which lower Z by 16; Z needs to fall by only 10, so 6 beta-minus emissions raise it by 6.

questions.q: The binding energy per nucleon is greatest for nuclei of mass number about
questions.explanation: The curve peaks near iron, at about 8.7 MeV per nucleon.

questions.q: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 2 days. The time needed for 87.5% of it to decay is
questions.explanation: 12.5% remains, which is (1/2)³, so three half-lives = 6 days.

questions.q: Taking E_n = -13.6/n² eV, the energy of the photon emitted when a hydrogen atom drops from n = 4 to n = 1 is
Compare alpha, beta and gamma radiations in terms of charge and penetrating power.
questions.answer: Alpha particles carry +2e and are stopped by paper; beta particles carry -e (or +e for positrons) and are stopped by a few millimetres of aluminium; gamma rays are uncharged and very penetrating, needing thick lead or concrete to be absorbed.
questions.explanation: Penetration falls as ionising power rises.

questions.q: A radioactive nuclide has a decay constant of 0.0693 per minute. Find its half-life and the fraction left after 30 minutes.
questions.explanation: The half-life is inversely proportional to the decay constant.

questions.q: The number of valence electrons in a silicon atom is
questions.explanation: Silicon is in group 14 and forms four covalent bonds.

questions.q: Which of the following is a suitable dopant for making an n-type semiconductor from silicon?
questions.explanation: Arsenic is pentavalent (donor); boron, indium and aluminium are trivalent acceptors.

questions.q: A half-wave rectifier is fed with 50 Hz AC. The frequency of the pulsating output is
questions.explanation: Only one half cycle per period is passed, so the output frequency equals the input frequency.

questions.q: In a forward-biased p-n junction, the current is mainly due to
options: majority carriers diffusing across the junction
minority carriers drifting across the junction
questions.explanation: Forward bias lowers the barrier so majority carriers cross in large numbers.

questions.q: A NOR gate has both of its inputs joined together. It then acts as a
questions.explanation: NOR(A, A) = (A + A)' = A', which is a NOT gate.

questions.q: A light emitting diode is made from a material with a band gap of 2.0 eV. The wavelength of the light it emits is about (hc = 1240 eV nm)
Explain how a p-n junction diode can be used as a rectifier.
questions.answer: A diode conducts when forward biased and blocks when reverse biased. With an AC input it conducts during one half cycle and blocks the other, so the output current flows in one direction only, converting AC to pulsating DC.
keyPoints: AC input gives unidirectional pulsating output
questions.explanation: Two or four diodes in a bridge make a full-wave rectifier.

questions.q: Write the truth table of a two-input NAND gate and explain why it is called a universal gate.
questions.answer: Outputs for inputs (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1) are 1, 1, 1, 0. NAND is universal because NOT (join the inputs), AND (NAND followed by NOT) and OR (NOT-ed inputs fed into a NAND) can all be built from NAND gates alone.
keyPoints: Output is 0 only when both inputs are 1
NOT is obtained by joining the inputs
AND and OR can be built from NAND gates, so any logic function is possible
questions.explanation: A single gate type that can build all others is called universal.
